limitations: This is a portal-token runtime acceptance sub-scope, not a complete manual caller/issuer review of the 202 authenticated-executable SECURITY DEFINER functions.
The 202-function allowlist remains blocked at 0/202 individually accepted; no entries in the global allowlist were changed.

Guest portal APIs are intentionally usable by anon with a valid portal token; a Supabase user JWT alone is not the portal credential. A legacy-Supabase-JWT denial case is not used as the acceptance criterion for this guest-token classification.
Per-RPC cross-participant coverage is recorded above; do not interpret a token-derived self-only API as having arbitrary target-IDOR coverage.

followUpFindings.description: Portal password lookup keys are currently derived from SHA-256 of the first eight password characters. Auto-generated temporary passwords use the format SK plus 12 hex characters, so the indexed lookup prefix has only 24 bits of entropy. The global UNIQUE(password_lookup_key) constraint can cause provisioning/regeneration collisions and fail a registration transaction.
followUpFindings.securityImpact: Not demonstrated as an authentication bypass: the full password is still verified with crypt(). The demonstrated concern is availability/integrity of credential provisioning and login lookup under scale.
followUpFindings.nextRequiredWork: Inventory every password_lookup_key writer/constraint/test; replace the truncated prefix with a full-password cryptographic lookup key (or equivalent collision-safe indexed design) consistently across writers/verifier; rehearse migration and provisioning of 5k+ synthetic participants on disposable PostgreSQL before rollout.
